response_summary: Verified HEAD fc6cf32 on main, clean worktree. Checked the live PokéAPI v2 /pokemon/{id} shape (id, name, sprites.front_default/front_shiny, sprites.other.official-artwork, types[].slot/type.name) and 404 behaviour before typing anything. Added src/types/pokemon.ts (PokemonSummary with id, apiName, sprites.normal/shiny, ordered types; PokemonBatch) and src/api/pokeApi.ts (constants for the 1–251 range and DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=30; isSupportedDexId; fetchPokemonById with a RangeError guard before any network call and PokeApiError on non-OK responses; fetchPokemonBatch({offset, limit}) that derives the ID window from offset/limit, clamps to #251, fetches only that window via Promise.all and returns items/offset/limit/total/hasMore). Raw PokéAPI types are private to the service. Rewrote src/app/pokedex.tsx to load the first batch with useState/useEffect (cancel flag on unmount), with explicit loading, error (+ Retry), empty and success states; success renders a FlatList of "#001 bulbasaur grass / poison" rows with zero-padded IDs and keeps the temporary /pokemon/197 Link. No search code. Checks: npm run lint clean; npx tsc --noEmit clean; npx expo export --platform android succeeded. Runtime check of the service against pokeapi.co: first batch 30 items in order #1–#30 with hasMore=true; offset 240 returns 11 items ending at celebi with hasMore=false; #197 = umbreon with official-artwork normal/shiny URLs; IDs 0/252, offset 251 and limit 0 all reject with RangeError.

decisions.suggestion: Call /pokemon?offset&limit list endpoint first, then fetch each result URL
decisions.reason: IDs 1–251 are contiguous and known, so the list round-trip adds latency without information; deriving the ID window from offset/limit and fetching /pokemon/{id} directly still follows the official v2 contract.

decisions.suggestion: Use sprites.front_default / front_shiny as the summary sprite URLs
decisions.reason: Prefer sprites.other.official-artwork (higher resolution, suited to the future card UI) and fall back to front_default/front_shiny; typed as string | null because PokéAPI can return null.

decisions.suggestion: Return an empty batch for offsets past #251 instead of throwing
decisions.reason: AC3 asks the service to reject out-of-range requests; throwing RangeError makes a caller bug visible instead of silently ending pagination. In-range batches that overrun the end are clamped (offset 240 → 11 items).

decisions.suggestion: Reset to the loading state with setState at the top of the useEffect
decisions.reason: eslint react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rejects synchronous setState in effects; initial state is already loading and the Retry handler now sets loading before bumping the attempt counter.

decisions.suggestion: Add a generic useFetch/useAsync hook or a PokemonCard component
decisions.reason: Speculative abstraction; prompt requires plain useState/useEffect in the route and PokemonCard is out of scope.

decisions.suggestion: Add fetchPokemonById as a public export
decisions.reason: It is the unit fetchPokemonBatch is built from, carries the range guard, and is exactly what the detail screen will need next; no extra code was added for it.

decisions.suggestion: Add unit tests for the range guards
decisions.reason: No concrete defect; guards were exercised against the live API in a throwaway script (recorded in response_summary) instead.

decisions.suggestion: Use a useRef mirroring heroId so the selection effect can read the current hero without a dependency
decisions.reason: eslint-config-expo enforces react-hooks/refs, which rejects reading ref.current during render; the ref-based variant failed npm run lint.

decisions.suggestion: Select the hero inside a useEffect and setHeroId from the effect body
decisions.reason: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect errors on a synchronous setState in an effect body; the selection is derived state, not external synchronization.

decisions.suggestion: Adjust hero selection during render, guarded by a selectedFor key holding the joined favorite ids
decisions.reason: React's documented derived-state pattern: the guard makes the random draw run once per favorite set, keeps the hero stable across re-renders (AC3), satisfies AC4 and AC10, and passes lint with no suppression.

decisions.suggestion: Track the hero fetch with a plain {status} state and set 'loading' at the start of the effect
decisions.reason: Tagging the result with the id it was requested for lets the loading state be derived when result.id !== heroId, so no setState runs synchronously in the effect and a stale result can never be shown for a new hero.

decisions.suggestion: Derive the hero purely from a session seed (index = seed * ids.length) to avoid state entirely
decisions.reason: Pure but unstable in practice: adding any unrelated favorite would shift the index and swap the hero, which AC3's stability intent argues against.

decisions.suggestion: Reuse PokemonCard for the hero
decisions.reason: PokemonCard is a compact 64px list row; AC6 requires a large accent-tinted hero with big artwork, so Home composes expo-image and TypeBadge directly and leaves the shared card untouched.

decisions.suggestion: Keep the Stack header on Home
decisions.reason: Home sets headerShown:false via a local <Stack.Screen> and pads with useSafeAreaInsets, so the hero reads full-bleed; _layout.tsx is left unchanged, so every other screen keeps its header.

decisions.suggestion: Persist the selected hero so it survives a restart
decisions.reason: Explicitly out of scope for this checkpoint; it would also add a second persistence surface next to the favorites store.

decisions.suggestion: Prefetch all favorite summaries so switching heroes is instant
decisions.reason: AC5 forbids loading all favorites to build Home; only the selected hero is requested.

decisions.suggestion: Add react-test-renderer and a unit test for hero selection
decisions.reason: The project has no test infrastructure and the checkpoint asks for structural verification; the selection loop was instead proven with a scratchpad simulation mirroring the component's render semantics.
